header: COMMON INDIAN NAMES, which I wrote out by hand for the search bar's "this looks like a name" hint (src/lib/search/nameHint/nameHint.ts). It is a hint only: a word missing here is simply not recognised as a name by this list (the plant's own name words, fetched from the directory, may still recognise it), and a word that is here but is not a name in a particular line only produces a hint that Enter would search people. I lean the lists on the regions the plant's people come from (Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the South and the West), in the spellings people actually write; the matching also folds spelling variants together (Goutam = Gautam, Sandip = Sandeep), so a spelling need not be listed twice. Upper case, letters only. Nothing here is about any real employee.

doc: I write family names as one word (Kumar, Singh, Mondal, Ghosh ... )

symbols.name: HONORIFICS
symbols.sig: const HONORIFICS: string[] = words(`MR MRS MS MISS SHRI SHREE SRI SMT SHRIMATI SRIMATI KUMARI DR ER ENGR PROF COL MAJ CAPT GEN LT`)
doc: words that stand before or after a name and are not part of it: Mr, Shri, Dr ... (I read a line that starts with one of them without it)

symbols.name: NAME_ENDINGS
symbols.sig: const NAME_ENDINGS: string[] = words(`KUMAR NATH PRASAD CHANDRA SHANKAR SANKAR NARAYAN RANJAN SINGH SINHA KANT KANTA BRATA JIT JEET`)
doc: I keep here the endings of the compound names written as one word (Ajaykumar, Motilal, Gopinath, Ramprasad, Sibshankar): a word of six letters or more that ends in one of these reads as a name (I left out endings that also end ordinary English words, like -pal in principal)
